## What Is Voice Dictation Software for Your Computer?


Voice dictation software for Mac and Windows converts spoken words into written text in real time. Whether you refer to it as speech to text software or voice to text software, the core benefit is the same. Press a hotkey, speak naturally, and your words appear in whatever app you're already using: Gmail, Slack, Google Docs, ChatGPT, or anything else.


This article covers live dictation tools only. These software tools go beyond recording calls after the fact, like Otter.ai or Fireflies meeting transcription services, and replace typing across your desktop.


Voice input can boost productivity by up to 30%. Professionals managing[carpal tunnel syndrome](https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/carpal-tunnel-syndrome/symptoms-causes/syc-20355603) (including those who need to know[when to switch from typing to voice](https://willowvoice.com/blog/typing-with-carpal-tunnel-when-to-switch-to-voice-input) ), those who find speaking more natural than typing, and people using[voice dictation for neurodivergent workflows](https://willowvoice.com/blog/voice-dictation-reduce-cognitive-load-adhd) all benefit, with little to no correction needed. Speaking at 150 words per minute vs. typing at 40 words per minute makes voice input over 3x faster.


### How to Choose the Right Dictation Software


-


**Platform:** Look for native Mac or Windows support, not virtualization workarounds.


-


**Accuracy needs:** Put custom vocabulary at the top of your list if you use technical, medical, or legal terms.


-


**Latency:** Target sub-300ms for fluid, real-time use.


-


**Privacy:** Require on-device processing or SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance for sensitive data.


-


**App coverage:** Choose a system-wide hotkey over a limited browser extension.


### Tips for Best Results from Any Dictation Tool


-


**Use a good microphone:** An external or headset microphone improves accuracy.


-


**Speak consistently:** Maintain a steady pace without shouting.


-


**Minimize noise:** Reduce background noise as much as possible.


-


**Add domain words:** Pre-load domain-specific words into your custom vocabulary.


-


**Speak first:** Get your thoughts out completely by voice, then edit later.

## Willow Voice vs. Wispr Flow: Key Differences


Willow Voice and Wispr Flow are the two most-compared AI dictation tools. On the key dimensions: Willow delivers ~200ms latency vs. Wispr Flow's ~700ms; an unlimited free plan vs. a ~2,000 words/week cap; shared custom dictionaries and admin controls vs. none; and full feature parity on Mac, Windows, and iOS vs. Mac and iOS primary. Both tools now hold SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA certifications, with Willow's zero data retention applied as a default across all plan tiers rather than unlocked at a higher price point.


For most professionals comparing AI dictation tools, the comparison comes down to five structural differences, not feature lists.


**Free plan.** Willow's free plan is genuinely unlimited with no word cap. Wispr Flow's free tier caps at roughly 2,000 words per week, a limit heavy users exhaust in a single working day. For a full breakdown of what that cap means in practice, see our guide to the[Wispr Flow free plan limits](https://willowvoice.com/blog/wispr-flow-free-plan-alternatives) . If you speak at 150 words per minute across a normal eight-hour workday, that cap disappears before Tuesday morning. Willow's free tier doesn't throttle you into a paid upgrade; it's the same AI voice engine with no artificial ceiling.


**Latency.** Willow processes at ~200ms; Wispr Flow runs at ~700ms. That gap, nearly 4x, is the difference between text appearing before your speaking rhythm is interrupted and text appearing after a pause long enough to lose the next thought. At 700ms, you finish a sentence, register the wait, then resume. At 200ms, the output keeps pace with natural speech. For professionals who speak in long bursts, emails, meeting notes, Slack threads, the compounding cost of that latency gap is real across a full day of use.


**Team features.** Willow includes shared custom dictionaries, admin controls, and team leaderboards for org-wide deployment. Wispr Flow has no shared dictionaries and no publicly documented admin console or team leaderboards. For an individual user, this distinction is invisible. For a team lead standardizing terminology across a group (client names, internal shorthand, product vocabulary), it's the difference between a tool that deploys at the individual level and one that deploys at the organizational level.


**Compliance.** Wispr Flow has expanded its compliance program to include SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA certifications, which meaningfully addresses prior gaps for regulated-industry teams. The architectural distinction that remains: Willow's zero data retention and SOC 2 Type II certification are defaults across all plan tiers, not features unlocked at a higher price point, and Wispr Flow routes audio through third-party AI providers, which introduces data residency questions for teams with strict handling requirements. For healthcare, legal, and finance teams, the compliance architecture matters before a single word is spoken.


**Cross-platform coverage.** Willow runs as a native app with full feature parity on Mac, Windows, and iOS: custom vocabulary, filler-word removal, and ~200ms latency on all three. Wispr Flow is Mac and iOS primary; Windows support exists but without the same feature depth. If your workflow spans a Windows workstation and a Mac laptop, that asymmetry creates gaps that compound over time.


## How to Choose the Right Voice Dictation Software


### Platform compatibility


Built-in tools are platform-locked: Apple Dictation runs on Mac only, Windows Voice Typing on Windows only, and Google Docs Voice Typing in Chrome only. If your work moves across Mac and Windows, or between desktop and mobile, a browser-only or OS-native tool creates gaps in your workflow. Look for a tool with native apps and full feature parity on every platform you use, not virtualization workarounds.


### Accuracy and custom vocabulary


Built-in dictation tools transcribe verbatim without learning from corrections, which means technical terms, proper nouns, and industry jargon misfire repeatedly. Tools like Willow Voice and Dragon support custom vocabulary layers that learn domain-specific terminology (variable names, medical terms, client names), so accuracy improves over time instead of degrading into a correction loop.


### Latency


Anything above ~500ms breaks speaking rhythm: you finish a sentence, pause, wait, then lose the next thought. Willow Voice processes at ~200ms, so text appears nearly instantly. Most alternatives, including built-in tools and several cloud-based options, run at 700ms or more, which creates a noticeable lag that disrupts natural dictation pace.


### Privacy and compliance


Healthcare, legal, and finance teams need more than a privacy policy. Look for SOC 2 Type II certification, zero data retention across all plans, and HIPAA support with signed Business Associate Agreements available. Willow Voice meets all three requirements and offers BAAs at the Enterprise tier, making it deployable in compliance-sensitive environments without a separate compliance review.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is speech-to-text software accurate enough for professional use?


Yes. Modern dedicated tools have closed the gap with human transcription. Willow Voice reaches 98%+ accuracy, including technical terms, proper nouns, and industry jargon, which is roughly 3x more accurate than built-in options like Apple Dictation or Windows Voice Typing. Filler-word removal further reduces manual cleanup, so the text that lands in your app is close to publish-ready without a correction loop.


### Does voice dictation software work offline?


It depends on the tool. Willow Voice offers an optional offline mode on Mac and iOS for situations where internet access is unavailable, though cloud mode delivers the fastest and most accurate results. Superwhisper takes a fully on-device approach, keeping all processing local with no audio sent to external servers, making it an option for users who require air-gapped privacy, at the cost of slower processing and lower accuracy compared to cloud-based tools.


### Is my audio data private?


Privacy policies vary widely across tools. Willow Voice operates with zero data retention across all plans: audio is processed and discarded, not stored, and it holds SOC 2 Type II certification with support for HIPAA-compliant workflows. Signed Business Associate Agreements are available at the Enterprise tier for healthcare organizations. If data residency and audit trails matter in your environment, verify the tool's compliance posture before deployment.


### Can I use speech-to-text on my phone?


Yes. Willow Voice offers a custom voice keyboard on iOS that delivers the same AI-powered dictation as the desktop version, including custom vocabulary, filler-word removal, and ~200ms latency, without reverting to Apple's default system keyboard. Custom vocabulary and settings sync automatically across Mac, Windows, and iOS, so terminology you've added on your desktop carries to your phone without any per-device configuration.


### How fast is voice dictation vs typing?


Most people speak at around 150 words per minute and type at around 40 words per minute, making voice input roughly 3x faster for capturing ideas, drafting emails, and writing messages. The net gain depends on accuracy: when a tool transcribes cleanly with minimal correction needed, the speed advantage holds. When accuracy is low and rework cycles eat into the time saved, the gap narrows considerably. High-accuracy tools with domain vocabulary support are where the net gain is real.
